source: NLS OS 25-inch (1:2500) 'london' layer XYZ tiles; over West Ham the Essex county series, 1893-96 revision (edition per sheet not verified)

edition_notes.status: INFERENCE from map content, 2026-09-28; sheet margins are cut off in the tiles, so no sheet number, survey or revision date was read directly. Verify against NLS sheet metadata before citing.
edition_notes.inferred_edition: Essex (or London) County Series 1:2500, most likely the 1893-96 revision (2nd edition), same epoch as the five-foot sheets; not the 1860s-70s first edition and probably not the c.1915 revision.
evidence: q18_131105_87125 (Manor Park / Little Ilford, E 542120 N 184752): Shelley Road, Byron Road and Woodhouse [Grove] are drawn as laid-out estate roads (pecked kerbs) with NO houses. That is the moment of 1890s estate layout: a 1860s-70s first edition would show only fields, and a c.1915 edition would show these streets built up.

q18_131111_87128 (E 542699 N 184483): the railway is lettered LONDON TILBURY & SOUTHEND RAILWAY with fields, Farm Lane and a few buildings; no suburban housing yet. Consistent with an early-1890s snapshot of East Ham; not diagnostic on its own.

q18_131105_87161 and q18_131108_87158 (Plaistow / East Ham levels, N 181300-181700): open grazing marsh with ditches, a straight embanked road (probably Beckton Road, c.1870) and a railway at the SE corner (probably the Beckton gasworks branch, 1870s). Proves post-1870; the marsh stayed open into the 1900s so this does not separate 1890s from later.
q18_131102_87149 / q18_131099_87152 (N 182100-182500): fields and a railway in cutting/embankment, parcel numbers with acreages to 3 dp; no West Ham tramways or new housing visible.
Hole mosaics are almost entirely undeveloped land (marsh, fields). That is probably WHY the five-foot London town plan has no sheets there: the 1:1056 was only published for built-up areas.
Sheet joins visible as thin straight lines with acreages repeated on both sides: horizontal at py ~780 in q18_131102_87149, vertical at px ~440 in q18_131105_87161 and px ~455 in q18_131105_87125.

Not seen in the mosaics examined: Royal Albert Dock (1880), Abbey Mills or LCC lettering, tram lines. The q18 set covers the hole east of the Channelsea plus edge rows, which lie away from those features.
edition_notes.datum: Heights read as feet above Ordnance Datum (Liverpool), as on the five-foot. Local B.M.s agree with the five-foot/1848 values in magnitude (e.g. marsh B.M.5.6, 5.7, 8.4; Manor Park B.M.32.4, 35.0).

reading_notes.digit_size_px: about 11-14 px tall at zoom 18 (upright acreages ~14 px, italic spot figures ~12-14 px, B.M. lettering ~11-13 px): about twice the five-foot 6 px
reading_notes.spot_heights: Whole feet, in small italic figures (e.g. 4, 8, 16, 31), written beside a small + or x or a dot on the road, path or bank; the survey point is that + / x / dot, not the figure. No decimal. Often regularly spaced along roads.
reading_notes.bench_marks: B.M. + pheon (broad arrow), to 1 dp (B.M.5.6, B.M.20.8, B.M.32.4); the pheon point is the position, usually on the line just beside the text.
reading_notes.look_alikes: Upright figures are parcel numbers (e.g. 104, 123) and acreages to 3 dp (4.818, 23.891, .653); never heights. B.S. = boundary stone, C.R. / C.S. = centre of road / stream (boundary), S.P. = signal post, B.P. = boundary post, triangle = trig/traverse station.
